subject: Banking
title: Why the Fed Was Created
description: A fast breakdown of Why the Fed Was Created for builders.

hook.text: The Panic of 1907 almost destroyed the US economy. One banker, J.P. Morgan, personally stopped the collapse.

buildup.text: Morgan locked bankers in his library and forced them to pool money to save failing banks. One man rescued the system.

discovery.text: Congress realized the nation couldn't depend on one private citizen. In 1913, they created the Federal Reserve System.

twist.text: The Fed was designed as 12 regional banks, not one central bank. Americans feared concentrated financial power.

climax.text: America's central bank was born from panic and distrust. It was built to prevent the crisis that created it.

punchline.text: One banker saved America in 1907. Congress decided never to need one man again.

quiz.question: What event led to the creation of the Federal Reserve?

details.summary: The Federal Reserve was created in 1913 after the Panic of 1907 demonstrated that the US needed a permanent central bank to prevent financial crises, provide elastic currency, and serve as a lender of last resort to the banking system.
details.whyItMatters: The Fed's creation was the most consequential financial reform in American history. Understanding why it was established explains its dual mandate, structure, and the political compromises that still shape monetary policy.
takeaways: The Panic of 1907 triggered the political momentum for a central bank
The Federal Reserve Act was signed by President Wilson on December 23, 1913
Its structure as a hybrid public-private institution was a political compromise

faq.question: Why did the US resist creating a central bank for so long?
faq.answer: Americans had deep distrust of centralized financial power dating to Andrew Jackson's destruction of the Second Bank. The Fed was structured as twelve regional banks rather than one central institution specifically to address these political concerns.

faq.question: What problems was the Fed designed to solve?
faq.answer: Recurring financial panics with no institution to provide emergency liquidity, seasonal currency shortages that disrupted agriculture and commerce, and the lack of a coordinated banking supervision system that allowed weak banks to threaten the entire system.
